result:
The proposed answer is most likely wrong. Its construction only shows that no threshold below roughly n/5 can work, and the upper-bound argument is only a sketch.

The C₅ blow-up does give a triangle-free graph with no rainbow C₄ and color degree about n/5 + 1. However, that only shows f(n) must be at least about n/5. It says nothing about whether a threshold near n/5 suffices.

The upper-bound section does not prove that n/5 suffices. It only asserts that the C₅ structure is the unique way to avoid a rainbow C₄, and it gives no argument for this.

I am working from memory of the literature, not a derivation. As I recall, the known theorem for rainbow C₄ in edge-colored triangle-free graphs has threshold (n+2)/3, and that bound is sharp. That threshold is well above n/5, which means there are better constructions than the C₅ blow-up with color degree near n/3. So (n+6)/5 cannot be the sharp bound.

VERDICT: REJECT
